quest.title: Solitary Sea-Beast
quest.description: Lost friends, extinct sea creatures... Is this a sad reminiscence, or the beginning of a new life?
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x300, Primogem x40, Hero's Wit x4, Mora x30000

dialogues.text: ...Ah, hello.
Sorry, I got a little distracted...
You guys are... unfamiliar faces. Sorry...I'm not very good at talking to strangers.
Ah... sorry... I didn't mean to be rude, I'm just... Sorry...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #Just call me {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's name is Paimon, nice to meet you!

dialogues.speaker: Kumi
dialogues.text: ...I'm Kumi, nice to meet you.

dialogues.speaker: Kumi
dialogues.text: Sorry, I just... rarely chat with people.

dialogues.speaker: Kumi
dialogues.text: May I ask... Is there anything I can help you with?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About this carcass...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We were just wondering, what animal carcass is this...?

dialogues.speaker: Kumi
dialogues.text: Oh...

dialogues.speaker: Kumi
dialogues.text: Her name is Kuntira, she's sort of... my childhood friend.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good...friend?

dialogues.speaker: Kumi
dialogues.text: This might sound silly... You may even think it's just my wishful thinking...

dialogues.speaker: Kumi
dialogues.text: This skeleton is what my childhood friend left behind.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Oh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Your friend was able to defeat such a huge sea creature... That's amazing!

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: Ahem...

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: I mean, these are the bones of my childhood friend. She's a sea creature.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh...

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: On Narukami Island — my father's hometown, people call these creatures "Umibouzu"...

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: It is also said that they often attack cargo ships on long voyages and will rob fishermen of their catch... So they are hunted down and killed by humans.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: But over here — my mother's hometown — the locals would give each individual creature a unique name.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: And she, my best friend... may have been the last of her kind.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Is that right...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow...

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: The people of Watatsumi never gave her species a common name.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: Because they think that... Just like us, each of them is a lonely individual.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: Lonely, docile, indifferent to curiosity and hostility outside of their own world...

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: Alone, roaming in the currents. Alone, suffocating in the shallows.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Huh...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How pitiful...

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: Don't think of it that way.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: Intentionally or not, when you say words like "how pitiful," you're alienating yourself from the other person and their experience. It dismisses and trivializes their pain.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: Only by empathizing with the other party's loneliness and pain, letting go of fear and defense, can we truly achieve understanding...

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: Perhaps that was why we happened to become friends back then.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: Rather than alleviating each other's loneliness, we were enjoying the loneliness together, a solitude we both shared.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: It's just that I have been away for a long time since I grew up. I finally had the opportunity to come back, only to realize that it's too late...

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: It's okay, don't let me affect your mood.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: Ah... excuse me, can you... Umm, never mind, it's nothing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's okay, just let us know!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Do you need our help?

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: ...Yes, sorry to bother the both of you.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: I came from Narukami Island wanting to visit her and stay here for a while...

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: But as you can see, my best friend has passed away. The way home is also blocked by the war... Maybe I'll be stranded even longer.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: I wanted to...at least offer something to my best friend. She loves Thunder Sakura flowers.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: But for safety reasons...I can no longer go back to the place where the Thunder Sakura grows.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: If I could ask you guys for help... I'd be ever so grateful.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: Thank you very much, umm... Be careful when passing through the non-safe areas. I will pray for you here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Miss Kumi, you're too polite!

dialogues.speaker: Kumi
dialogues.text: ...Ah, sorry, I didn't expect you guys to be back so soon.

dialogues.speaker: Kumi
dialogues.text: Do you need anything...?

choices.text: I brought what you asked for.
It's nothing, we're still trying to look for the petals.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: Thank you for your hard work, it's good to take a break here.

dialogues.speaker: Kumi
dialogues.text: Thank you so much! I knew I could count on you guys!

dialogues.speaker: Kumi
dialogues.text: ...Mm, these are enough to make a wreath of flowers, thank you once again.

dialogues.speaker: Kumi
dialogues.text: By the way... I have one more thing I want to ask of you, I don't know if you guys mind...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Since we've already helped you out, feel free to tell us, Miss Kumi!

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: ...It's like this. I heard from the elders of Bourou Village that there is hilichurl activity again on the beach to the west.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: It so happens that a researcher from Sumeru passed by here the other day and is heading there... I think her name is Anisa, and she hasn't returned yet.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: I'm quite worried about her...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That researcher... Is she your friend?

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: Are friends the only ones worth worrying about?

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: Sorry, I mean... I don't really know her well, but I'm just worried.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: Sorry to trouble you again... If it weren't for the fact that I can't handle myself in fights...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's okay, you don't have to blame yourself! Let's just go help!

talks.objective: Head to the hilichurl camp in the west

dialogues.speaker: Anisa
dialogues.text: *panting* Phew... Thank you, if it weren't for your help, I'm afraid I would be dead...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No need to thank us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're Anisa, right? Miss Kumi asked us to come!

dialogues.speaker: Anisa
dialogues.text: Kumi...? Oh! It's that...local lass who looks a bit gloomy but is very nice, right?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Lass...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What a strange and flippant way of describing her...

dialogues.speaker: Anisa
dialogues.text: Hehe... Actually, I forgot her name. I really shouldn't have. I'll have to thank her properly later on.

dialogues.speaker: Anisa
dialogues.text: Oh, yes, her name is "Kumi," right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right! You shouldn't be a researcher with a memory like that!

dialogues.speaker: Anisa
dialogues.text: Yes, I remember this time! Kumi, that's a cute name. Kumi...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: *coughing*

dialogues.speaker: Anisa
dialogues.text: Ah, sorry, I didn't introduce myself, although you might already know...

dialogues.speaker: Anisa
dialogues.text: I'm Anisa. Anisa Purbiruni. Trainee Dastur at Sumeru Akademiya's Oceanographic Society.

dialogues.speaker: Anisa
dialogues.text: As for my surname, Purbiruni, it's because my academic lineage dates back five centuries to the great scholar, the sage Biruni.

dialogues.speaker: Anisa
dialogues.text: Ah, every time I mention this, a pride that cannot be expressed in words wells up within me unbidden!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Man, she's like some rich girl bragging about her dad's money...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Kumi's very worried about you.

dialogues.speaker: Anisa
dialogues.text: Hehe...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What are you laughing about?

dialogues.speaker: Anisa
dialogues.text: Nothing... I'm just a little embarrassed about making people worry about me...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's surprised that you can be embarrassed at all!

dialogues.speaker: Anisa
dialogues.text: However, there are still things that I have yet to do. The research I have on hand has not yet borne fruit, and so I must hurry.

dialogues.speaker: Anisa
dialogues.text: You know, the statues of Watatsumi here are the object of my research. The traditional beliefs of the people of Watatsumi are very fascinating.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh?

dialogues.speaker: Anisa
dialogues.text: In antiquity, the priests... uh, I mean, shrine maidens of Watatsumi would place permanently-given offerings under memorials.

dialogues.speaker: Anisa
dialogues.text: After that, they would protect those offerings with sophisticated mechanical puzzles or simple elemental techniques.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What?

dialogues.speaker: Anisa
dialogues.text: This was originally a manner of protecting and storing objects that were offered...

dialogues.speaker: Anisa
dialogues.text: But people gradually discovered the joys of solving puzzles for their own sake, and even considered this a way of communicating with the now-deceased through one's intellect.

dialogues.speaker: Anisa
dialogues.text: As such, the solving of puzzles became melded together with religious rituals, resulting in a most unique tradition.

dialogues.speaker: Anisa
dialogues.text: As such, apart from the usual offerings, "solving puzzles left by those who came before" and seeking the "desires of the heart" also became rituals of worship or divination.

dialogues.speaker: Anisa
dialogues.text: Of course, the better part of this is my personal guesswork. If we want to be sure, we'll need to conduct a great deal of folklore studies.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, these "desires of the heart" are actually...

dialogues.speaker: Anisa
dialogues.text: It's as you've guessed. I'm referring to the riches offered to the statues of Watatsumi — the gifts of forebears to their descendants.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Riches!

dialogues.speaker: Anisa
dialogues.text: By which I mean treasure, of course — treasure!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Treasure!

dialogues.speaker: Anisa
dialogues.text: Your little companion seems to have a strong interest in my topic of study. How about it, then? Interested in lending me a hand?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Come on, there's treasure! Let's just help out, shall we?

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: As for me, I'm not all that interested in treasure. I just need my research results.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: It'll be great if you're willing to help. The treasure's all yours. Consider it your payment for helping me out!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Woohoo!

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Woohoo!

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Oh, don't worry. Let's start right here!

dialogues.speaker: Kumi
dialogues.text: Hello there. Thanks for bringing Anisa back safe and sound.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Hello there, Little... uh, Miss Kumi. Sorry for making you worry.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: I'm just glad to see that you're all right. I've just finished my garland, too.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: Sorry for taking up your time. Let me give her this garland...

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Mm, please go ahead.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: Thank you.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: I hope that my feelings, though late, will get through to her.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: I'm... all alone again...

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: What was her name?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh, why are you suddenly asking that?

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: I hear that the people of Watatsumi give each individual a unique name.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: If you don't mind me asking, what was your friend's name?

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: Kuntira.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: That's a lovely name.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: Thank you...

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: The elders on the island say that "kuntira" means "whale" in the ancient language.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: But I chose this name because I like it...

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Well, it also fits with "Kumi," doesn't it? It's a lovely name!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (What's she doing!?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Best we avoid disturbing them, Paimon.)

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: Um, thank you.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: *cough* Apologies. I spoke a little out of turn.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: That's okay.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: She was the last remnant of their kind. She was born alone, and she died alone.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: Born in the sea, dying on land where she didn't belong, suffocating in the air...

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: Recently I've been thinking, sooner or later, this might be my destiny as well.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: It's not like that.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: There's no need to persuade me... I understand what you're thinking... but after all, you and I are not the same...

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: I wasn't born here, nor do I belong to my father's hometown...

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: No, I was talking about the pelvic bones.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Yes, the pelvic bones.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Pelvic bones...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Pelvic bones? What are you talking about?

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: *cough* It's like this...

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Have you guys noticed, that unlike a whale, she still has well-developed pelvic bones.?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Not at all... How did you notice?

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Since I first arrived here, I have been paying attention to its pelvic structure... and the traces it left behind. I suppose you can call this an academic's instinct, hehe.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Hmmm...for example, when we give birth, we experience strong expansions and contractions, and as such, a stable support structure that protects our internal organs and soft tissues is indispensable.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Our pelvis is the structure that performs this function, and for Kuntira, her pelvis is the same.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Oh...

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: A pelvis that has undergone childbirth tends to show a certain degree of deformation and wear due to expansion and contraction.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: The body shape of primitive marine creatures tends to be teardrop-shaped, so their pelvises are also narrower.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: In other words, the marks of pelvic deformation are more obvious and easier to observe.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: Hmmm...is that so?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Oh...

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Ah, sorry, I've just been talking about common knowledge. I suppose I've been boring you all to death.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: Oh no, please continue...

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: You have a very beautiful tone of voice, at least. Has anyone ever told you that?

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Uhm... Thank you... I never noticed... *cough* *cough* Um, thanks.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Ahem... Back to the topic at hand... As such, I have grounds to fully refute your reasoning.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Based on the deformations of the pelvic bones, she must have undergone many births. It seems she had found her home in the sea, and...

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: She had more than one offspring...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow...

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Hmmm, in other words, she found her own happiness.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: But if that's the case...then why would she...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Stay stranded here...?

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Haha, that's your second mistake, Miss Kumi.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Stranded sea animals often show signs of distortion and strain on certain parts of their vertebrae.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: If you must know why, it's because suffocating is... very painful.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: But based on my preliminary observations, Kuntira's spine is straight, almost as if she did not experience any painful struggle...

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Based on a rough observation of her bone age, I would estimate that she passed away safely before she came to shore...

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: As for why she came to this familiar place in her final hours...

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Maybe this was her way of telling her good friend that she had lived a happy and fulfilling life.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: Thank you.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: So, you've got to live well, too.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: Yes... I will.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: ...You know, I would always feel torn as to whether I should return to my home on Narukami Island or to stay here in Bourou Village...

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Before, I was also torn whether to head back to Akademiya or stay in this country.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Due to the war, confusion, the pressure from the Shogunate...it's all too much, and many people have considered giving up.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: But one must make a choice, to continue or to give up. Choosing to continue may still wind up being fruitless, but choosing to give up...

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: I won't give up.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: When it's war or government, they're just another problem. This is another matter entirely...

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Haha, you're right!

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Think about it, hundreds of years later when people talk about this war, they can only lament the tragedy it caused and how meaningless it all was.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: But when they talk about the history of Watatsumi Island, about your friends, and you and me, they will remember...

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: That this island had a daredevil that stumbled out and somehow unlocked some of the truths behind our history?

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Yes, and that there also lived a girl who befriended a giant sea creature, and thus decided where her home should be.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: When she was young, when she first met me, I had a similar feeling... the feeling that my life was only just beginning.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Then let your life begin once again — this time, without any fear of loss.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Ohh, Paimon's getting mad! We were running all these errands for them, and here they are, chatting away!)

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Uh, having said that, there is one thing that I must ask you, Miss Kumi.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow... You're so formal all of a sudden!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: She's got some other agenda, huh...

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: I might have to stay on Watatsumi Island to study marine life in the long term... So in the meantime, could I, uh...

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: Do you mean that you want to... study Kuntira's children?

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: No, I want to try making friends with her children.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: And... if you don't mind, Miss Kumi— Well, it's at your convenience, of course, I wouldn't want to...

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: I live in Bourou Village. I'm sure I could give you a room, as long you're alright with it.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: I'd love to meet her children as well. Maybe that was what she wanted me to see — the family that she cared about.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Thank you!

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: And there's no need to learn how to speak as we do. I think you speak beautifully as it is.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Hehe... Well then, thanks a lot, Lit— I mean, Miss Kumi!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh... It feels like we've been left out in the cold.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: #Thank you so much for you help as well, {NICKNAME}, Paimon. I will not forget this.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Hehe, me too! My future lectures will always have seats open for you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? No, Paimon's not here to study!

choices.text: It is how it is, Paimon.
I only did as I should've.

talks.objective: Solve the puzzle of the Watatsumi statue

dialogues.speaker: Anisa
dialogues.text: Well then, congratulations are in order!

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Haha, it's fine. It's like I said, this is a symbol of "the heart's desire."

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: The forebears of this land left it to those who came after, as a symbol of faith and a token of trust. In fact, hmm, you could consider it a concrete way of "passing memories on."

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: So be at ease and just take it. It's yours by right.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: The people of Watatsumi understood this very early on: the fruits of wisdom are to be given to those who respect it.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: ...Just like you and me!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Does Paimon count too?

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Of course! Thanks for your hard work!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You're most welcome.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, no need to be so formal!

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: *sigh* Still, this thesis I'm working on is such a headache.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? Didn't you have a breakthrough already?

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Well, yes. But I've spent far too much time on just one subject.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: To formally become a Dastur as opposed to remaining a trainee, you need to have two different theses pass through the review stage...

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: I can ask for an extension, of course, but I do still need to find a second topic.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: My second field of study is actually marine biology, but due to the recent instability in Inazuma, I've had to call a halt to research on that front.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Eh? What is it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh right! Miss Kumi's good friend!

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Huh? Haha, I don't think she and I have gotten that far yet...

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Eh!? Oh... Oh right! I remember now!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What does this person fill their brain with, Paimon wonders...

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: I actually had a passing glance at that creature earlier. If I'm not mistaken, the skeleton is that of an Umibouzu — or at least, that's what the people of Narukami Island call it.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: They are huge, intelligent and savage sea monsters, and were once considered the arch-nemesis of all sailors.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: They were overly clever and overly proud... Just like us humans. I suppose that's why they came into conflict with us and became savage beasts.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: These sea creatures have been all but wiped out in most ocean regions, but it seems that this isn't the case here...

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: It seems as though they've even grown close to humanity. This is a very unusual phenomenon indeed. Very interesting.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Thanks a lot! I knew I was right to call on you two for help.

response.speaker: Anisa
response.text: Well, time's a-wasting here. Let's head back and look for Miss Kumi!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup, let's go!

choices.text: Paimon's talking about a sea creature.

dialogues.speaker: Kumi
dialogues.text: Can I help you with anything?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Anisa...

dialogues.speaker: Kumi
dialogues.text: She's a researcher from Sumeru. She's rather reckless, but she has a beautiful voice...

dialogues.speaker: Kumi
dialogues.text: She said that her field of study was Oceanic Sanctuary Storage... something. I'm not sure what that's about, really.

dialogues.speaker: Kumi
dialogues.text: But she seems to be very interested in that Watatsumi statue on the beach to the west...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Watatsumi statue?

dialogues.speaker: Kumi
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm. The village elder used to say that if we could solve the shrine maiden's puzzle, then "our heart's desire" would emerge.

dialogues.speaker: Kumi
dialogues.text: Hehe, I used to believe that. Everyday, I would swim near that statue... That was actually how I met my good friend as well.

dialogues.speaker: Kumi
dialogues.text: But I grew out of that a long time ago. I no longer believe in those stories.

dialogues.speaker: Kumi
dialogues.text: Still, I can't help but feel happy for Anisa — that she still has so much interest and passion regarding these old legends.

dialogues.speaker: Kumi
dialogues.text: I hope that she finds what she seeks...

dialogues.speaker: Kumi
dialogues.text: Well, but before that, please find out if she's alright. Thank you very much.

dialogues.speaker: Kumi
dialogues.text: Ah, it's you. Is there anything else I can help you with?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We found Anisa.

dialogues.speaker: Kumi
dialogues.text: Oh, thank you. How is she?

choices.text: She's in one piece and then some.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: Mmm, as long as she's alright... She can be really reckless, and it's very worrying.

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: I know that we're still practically strangers, but I wouldn't want to see anyone get hurt needlessly, especially at times like these...

response.speaker: Kumi
response.text: Also, she... Never mind...

choices.text: She's just busy with her research topic.

dialogues.speaker: Anisa
dialogues.text: It's fine if you can't solve it for now. The puzzle isn't going to run away or anything!

dialogues.speaker: Anisa
dialogues.text: I'll be here too — so just relax.
